newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse media profit falls in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse media profit falls in second quarter.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. on Monday reported a $1 million profit for the second quarter after recording a loss of $89 million in the year-earlier period, but operating profits at its core media business fell.

Still, analysts said Westinghouse was doing well at strengthening its media operations in preparation for the company's split in September. The Pittsburgh-based conglomerate plans to split its media businesses from its industrial businesses to form separate companies.

"They've got nothing to cry about and a lot to feel good about," said John Reidy at brokerage Smith Barney. "They're at the top of the heap in the radio business and they've been making good progress with their television stations, a little sooner than some would have expected."

The second-quarter profit, equal to nil per share, came on revenues of $2.4 billion, up from $2.1 billion a year earlier. The loss in the 1996 quarter equalled 20 cents a share, when the company took an after-tax charge of $114 million, or 26 cents per share.
Operating profit in the media business fell almost 20 percent, to $155 million from $192 million. Total media sales rose 17 percent to $1.28 billion from $1.10 billion.

For the latest quarter, Westinghouse said its media group, which includes the CBS television and radio networks, as well as Infinity Broadcasting, reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, of $261 million. That compared with $340 million in the year-earlier quarter, on a proforma basis.

Infinity's contribution for the quarter was offset by decreased revenue at the television network and a less favourable effect of purchase price accounting for programme rights. On a proforma basis, sales in the media group were essentially flat.
CBS Radio posted EBITDA of $157 million, about 23 percent above a year ago on a proforma basis. But television stations revenues declined 4 percent on a comparable station basis.
Reidy said CBS continued to post solid ratings and gained market share in late-night newscasts in large markets, including New York, Los Angeles and Chicago.
During the quarter, Westinghouse combined its radio and television groups into a consolidated CBS Station Group and took steps to improve advertising sales in its local markets.

Westinghouse said financial performance improved in every business in its industrial group. Power Systems boosted revenues to $838 million in the latest quarter vs. $732 million a year earlier. Operating profit was $1 million vs. a loss of $35 million a year ago.

Thermo King, a transport refrigeration unit, posted operating profit of $49 million on revenues of $263 million, vs. $46 million on $265 million in sales a year earlier. Profitability was enhanced by higher bus air conditioning sales, improved conditions in the North American truck and trailer industry, lower material costs and productivity improvements.
Westinghouse's stock slipped 50 cents to $23.875 in consolidated, afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
